newsitem.title: UK: Cellnet quarterly new subscribers dive.
newsitem.headline: Cellnet quarterly new subscribers dive.

text.p: Cellnet, Britain's second biggest mobile telephone company, on Wednesday reported only 12,000 net new connections over the last three months, blaming tighter credit controls and new contract terms for the decrease in market growth.
Cellnet, which is 60 percent owned by British Telecommuncations Plc and 40 percent by Securicor Group Plc, connected a net new 81,000 subscribers in the comparative period in 1996, analysts say.
Since the company's managing director Howard Ford left the group unexpectedly last month, rumours have swept the market that Cellnet has performed poorly.

Cellnet said new contract terms introduced for many new customers during the last quarter, reducing their notice period down to one month, and tighter credit controls on both new and existing customers had led to a short term decrease in net connections.
"Together, these actions contributed an estimated 70,000 additional disconnections in the quarter," the company stated.
Cellnet said that its customer base had grown to 2.7 million, a 13 percent increase of 309,000 over the year to date.

Analysts had expected disappointing subscriber figures from the company as it concentrates on migrating customers from its older analogue network onto its newer digital system at the expense of attracting new subscribers.
"They are running faster to stand still," noted Oliver Ehrenberg, telecoms analyst at Robert Fleming.

Cellnet's new net subscribers figures lag far behind those of its three rivals. But some analysts say BT, which is keen to buy out Securicor, may use the figures to barter a bargain price for the holding, which is valued at between 1.2 and 1.6 billion stg.

BT is currently restricted by regulators from buying the Cellnet stake because of competition concerns, but analysts expect that restriction to be lifted amid increasing competition in the British telecoms market.
Vodafone Group Plc, the mobile 'phone market leader that is also migrating customers to its digital network, has reported 67,000 net new customers in the last quarter.

But the winners in the race to connect new customers are the two smaller, purely digital services -- Britain's youngest mobile 'phone operator Orange Plc and, to a lesser extent, One 2 One, jointly-owned by Cable and Wireless Plc and U S West Inc.
Orange earlier reported a hefty 109,000 net new subscribers, while One 2 One said it had connected a net new 75,000 in the quarter.
